<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/">What belongs in Core</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Core means always present. Six ordered tests place a candidate into one of five outcomes, and the roster records every one.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#core-means-always-present"><code>Core</code> means always present, so nothing outside Tier 0 may register a name under it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#tier-placement">A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#five-placements">A candidate lands in exactly one of five placements: Core, Native, Ext, Dropped or answered</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#tier-roster">Every subsystem's tier is recorded once in the roster, including the ones no milestone has built</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#reserved-namespace">The <code>Core</code> namespace is the compiler's: nothing may declare under it and its rosters are closed while compiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun">A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/">Naming and shape</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Twenty shape rules every member obeys: the subject first, a verb that predicts the return type, and casing that is a hard error.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#shape-rules">Every <code>Core</code> member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#subject-first">The subject is parameter 1 of every <code>Core</code> member, with no exceptions</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#verb-lexicon">A member's verb predicts its return type, and <code>…OrNull</code>, <code>…Safe</code>, <code>…Ex</code> and every <code>try…</code> but <code>tryParse</code> are banned</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#symmetric-names">A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#one-name-one-signature">One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#members-are-full-words">A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#identifier-casing">An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#casing-checks-the-leading-character">Only the leading character's case is checked, so <code>HTTPClient</code> and <code>HttpClient</code> both pass</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#casing-has-no-suppression">There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/">Everything is written down</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Visibility, wire-format participation and qualifier behaviour are all declared. Nothing about a member is inferred structurally.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#written-visibility">Every member declaration writes exactly one visibility keyword, and there is no implicit <code>public</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair">An asymmetric property writes both halves, so a bare <code>private(set)</code> does not compile</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#legacy-property-shapes-name-the-visibility"><code>var $x;</code> and a bare <code>int $x;</code> in a class body report the missing visibility, not a statement error</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#a-parameter-is-not-a-member">A constructor parameter is not a member, because visibility is what promotes one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#written-participation">A class participates in a wire format only where it writes so, never structurally</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/everything-is-written/#qualifier-behaviour-is-declared">Every <code>Core</code> member declares whether it is a sink, a launderer, contagious or neutral</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/">One way to do each thing</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Nothing mutates, nothing reads ambient state, no mutable twin, no mode string, no encoding argument, one range convention.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#nothing-mutates">No <code>Core</code> member mutates its argument and none takes a reference</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-mutable-immutable-twins">Every <code>Core</code> value type is immutable, so no mutable twin exists to choose between</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-ambient-state">No <code>Core</code> member reads ambient state: there is no default timezone, locale, array pointer or error global</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#failure-throws">A <code>Core</code> member throws on failure and returns <code>?T</code> for absence; <code>false</code> is never an answer</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-paradigm-per-operation">No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays">A scalar and an <code>array&lt;T&gt;</code> never gain methods</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-mode-strings">A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#units-are-types">A unit is a type: a duration is a <code>Duration</code> and a size is <code>uint</code> bytes</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-encoding-argument">A <code>string</code> member never takes an encoding argument</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-range-convention">Every range is <code>(offset, ?length)</code>, and a negative counts from the end</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>

<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/">Parameters and the options bag</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>

<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/">Shape parameters</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One checked type with disjoint arms, flattened away at the ABI so no shape exists at run time.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#field-wise-precedence">Where the registry and the spec both describe an implemented member, precedence is field by field</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#shape-parameter">A fixed-key shape parameter is one type carrying its arms, and it is only ever a whole parameter</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#shape-arms-are-disjoint">A shape's arms are pairwise disjoint, so exactly one accepts a written literal and no field is declared a discriminant</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#one-checked-shape-type">The options bag and the shape parameter are two registry spellings of one checked type</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#shape-flattens-at-the-abi">A shape argument flattens into one argument per field of the merged list, so no shape exists at run time</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/shape-parameters/#shape-reuses-the-option-diagnostics">A shape key reuses the options bag's two diagnostics, and a missing required key is an ordinary type mismatch</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
